Definition: from G303 and ἵημι (to send); to let up, i.e. (literally) slacken or (figuratively) desert, desist from:--forbear, leave, loose.
BiblicalUsage: The prison doors are opened and the bands loosed at Philippi, and the writer of Hebrews promises God will never leave us nor forsake us. The word means to slacken, to let go, to leave off.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for letting go carries no doctrine of its own; its comfort is Hebrews', that the God who never leaves us is the reason we can loosen our grip on fear.
RelatedEvents: Paul and Silas in the Philippian Prison
